newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Mixed tone seen in major indexes.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Mixed tone seen in major indexes.

text.p: No clear direction was evident in major U.S. stock index options trading Tuesday, with investors playing both sides of the market as it recovered from early losses to move higher, traders said.
By about 1120 CDT/1620 GMT, the Dow industrial average DJI was up 18 points at 7,790 after falling in early trading to about 7,703.
The S&P 500 index was up 1.30 at 895.20. It fell to 886.19 but rebounded to post a new record intraday high at 897.03. September S&P 500 futures were up 1.35 at 905.50.
The S&P 100 index gained 2.70 to 875.07. It had fallen to 864.96 before rebounding to strike a new record intraday high at 876.86.
"There's been one big trade, but other than that it's been back and forth," said Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in the OEX.
Traders said a U.S. brokerage firm was a big seller of the July 900 calls, which had volume of about 4,700 contracts.
One OEX trader said the way the market is going, those calls will most likely be in-the-money soon, but the seller probably got long S&P 500 futures to hedge the position.
"I don't see any downward turn in the near future," the trader said. "I don't see any reason for one, but maybe if enough people think that, we'll finally get one."
Callahan said the market could be in for a short period of sideways consolidation, with no major economic data due and Friday's expiration of June options the main highlight.
But even the expiration may turn out to be a non-event.
"More often than not, that's moved away from the actual day," he said. "By tomorrow it will probably be out of the way. We're probably in for a breather here."
Fairly heavy action in OEX and SPX options suggested some expiration-related business was being done, traders said.
By 1130 CDT/1630 GMT, OEX call volume was 49,217 contracts and put volume was 45,844. In the SPX, put volume was 53,918 compared to call volume of 37,915.
Traders said volatilities were little changed so far on the day, with solid action on both the call and put side from buyers and sellers.
The CBOE's volatility index was up 0.27, or 1.2 percent, at 23.15, having ranged from 22.53 to 23.61.
Volatility "looks to be reflecting where we've been and where we're going and when the market goes sideways, volatility will naturally come in," Callahan said.
The trader, who was off last week, said the most difficult part of returning to the trading floor was adjusting not to the volatility but to new pricing levels.
"We're 60 or 70 points higher (in S&P 500 futures) than when I left," he said.
